slides.headline: She moved to America at 20 with $200. Now she's building the world's longest-range electric boat.
Sampriti Bhattacharyya founded Navier, an electric hydrofoil boat company
slides.body: Born in Kolkata, she moved to the US at 20 with just $200 and later earned a PhD in Mechanical Engineering from MIT in 2017, with career stops at NASA, Fermilab and TIFR. Her first venture, Hydroswarm, an ocean-robot startup, didn't succeed - she founded Navier in 2019 anyway.

slides.headline: America's first electric hydrofoiling boat - ten times more efficient than gas-powered ones.
slides.body: Navier's N30 is the world's longest-range electric vessel, gliding four feet above the water on carbon foils that cut drag and wake while boosting speed. It runs roughly ten times more efficiently than a comparable gas-powered boat, in an industry Bhattacharyya sees as still running on legacy fleets.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: One failed startup didn't end the story. It funded the education for the one that worked.
slides.body: A Viksit Bharat by 2047 needs builders who treat failure as data, not verdict. Bhattacharyya's first company folded - her second is now reshaping an entire industry most people assumed couldn't change.

sources.text: Robb Report - How Sampriti Bhattacharyya Launched a Top U.S. Boatbuilding Company
